doc: قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (106) لسنة 2022 بشأن اللائحة التنفيذية للمرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم (9) لسنة 2022 بشأن عمال الخدمة المساعدة.pdf
symptom: Document 106 does NOT have a persistence/write-barrier issue (contradicting the task description's misreading of line 103). Artifacts successfully persist and are scoreable with measurable char counts in both Run 18 and Run 19. The MARGINAL verdict is driven by two stable issues: (1) structural collapse (depth 0/1 flat tree, 0 structural markers detected), and (2) low OCR char density (~1690 chars/page, just above the 1500 floor but well below expected 2000-4000 for a 15-page legal regulation). This differs from وارد 597 (ERROR, truly absent artifacts) and world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf (ERROR, truly absent artifacts).
root_cause: OCR quality limitation, not persistence/write-barrier failure. Document 106 is a 15-page scanned Arabic legal regulation (zero text layer, fully image-based). Tesseract/Docling OCR produces marginal-quality markdown with thin text extraction (~1690 chars/page) and critically, missing structural heading markers (المادة, الباب, etc.) that the LLM-based md_to_tree needs to build hierarchical structure. The pipeline correctly detects this as marginal via (a) suspect_density gate check (1690/1690 chars/page marginally passes the 1500-floor but indicates suboptimal extraction), and (b) tree quality measure of depth=0/1 for a document that should have depth 3-4 article/chapter hierarchy. The RFC-029 D4 retry-arbitration bug (client.py:1083-1147) that caused Run 13 FAIL (2022 chars) was fixed before Run 18 (25k chars recovered), but no secondary OCR recovery mechanism exists beyond Tesseract. Docling's force_full_page_ocr=True is the only escalation path, and it produces insufficient quality for this document type.
code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py:1126-1127 (MIN_SCANNED_DENSITY_FLOOR constant), 1432-1433 (suspect_density gate), 874-919 (_is_garbled_blob), 1308-1443 (validate_tree); src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:74-87 (Arabic structural marker detection), lines 45-53 (_relevel_headings); src/pageindex_mcp/client.py:2202-2255 (_run_md_to_tree, tree-building via LLM). The structural collapse is NOT a code defect but an architectural limitation: the LLM's markdown-to-tree conversion depends on input markdown quality, and OCR from scanned PDFs produces insufficient heading structure markers.
suggested_fix: This document cannot be fixed with targeted code changes to the current pipeline. It requires one of: (A) SECONDARY OCR RECOVERY: implement a fallback mechanism beyond Tesseract (e.g. EasyOCR, PaddleOCR with Arabic support, or a higher-confidence/higher-quality commercial OCR tier) when Tesseract output is thin/marginal; (B) HEADING RECONSTRUCTION: inject synthetic structural markers (مادة, الباب patterns) into the markdown before tree-building when detected as missing, based on document layout analysis; or (C) DOCUMENT TYPE ROUTING: pre-classify Arabic legal documents and apply specialized heading-extraction logic (e.g. docling-hierarchical-pdf equivalent for Arabic legal gazette numbering, per the converters.py:80-100 comment showing Arabic legal structures are recognized but never promoted to headings). The current Tesseract route (Docling with force_full_page_ocr=True) is the only escalation and is insufficient. Between Runs 13-19 this document remained MARGINAL across all runs once the RFC-029 D4 bug was fixed; no further improvement has occurred, confirming the issue is structural/architectural, not a transient regression.
